items.evidence: horizon-items/src/items.rs LootContext: (1) condition() (line 2070) reads the kind ONLY from o.get("type") (line 2075) — no dual-form read; 26.1's data uses the "condition" key throughout (1,545 occurrences, 0 type-keyed), so every object condition's kind is "" and the match falls to _ => false. conditions() (line 2196) consults the plural "conditions" array, but every element fails. (2) evaluate() applies pool["modifier"]/table["modifier"] (lines 1957-1958), expand() pushes e["modifier"] (line 2230), nested() applies entry["modifier"] (line 2371) — 26.1's data has ZERO "modifier" keys and puts functions in "functions" arrays (983: 964 entry/10 pool/9 table), so no function ever runs; modifiers()'s own dual-form discriminator read (f["type"].or(f["function"]), line 2395) is dead code. No normalisation in the load path (loot.rs load_dir lines 773-790 parses files straight into the shared map). Impact over all 1,326 tables: 1,192 carry >=1 condition or >=1 function — blocks 1,052/1,085 (1,023 with a condition), entities 62/108, chests 54/56, gameplay 6/26, dispensers 3/3, equipment 3/3, spawners 3/5, shearing 3/22, harvest 2/3, archaeology 1/6, carve 1/1, charged_creeper 1/6, pots 1/1; only 134 tables roll correctly. Survival path traced: Game::block_loot_at (game.rs:5084) -> block_drops_by_player (game.rs:3697/3699, items.rs:1646) -> block_drops_raw -> ctx.evaluate (items.rs:1755) — every conditioned pool/entry is dropped, so survival block-breaking drops nothing from conditioned tables (same symptom the owner confirmed in-game for 1.21.7). /loot routes all table types through this engine too. Post-fix residual recorded here: modifiers() has 12 arms and is missing 7 of the 19 function kinds in the data (copy_components 71 block tables, furnace_smelt 16 entity, set_enchantments 4, set_stew_effect 3, exploration_map 3, set_ominous_bottle_amplifier 3, set_instrument 1 — union 101 tables), and expand() (line 2211) has no minecraft:tag arm (the single tag entry, entities/creeper.json); union + tag = 102 tables, exactly the 26.2 run's B12-G01 count. The 26.2 tree reads ["functions"] + dual-form discriminators (items.rs:1969-1970/2246/2387, loot.rs:1386/1507/1534/2040/2042/2053/2097/2153) — the 26.2 playtest fixes were never carried to 26.1. Canonical engine item for the merge: Batch 4's B4-G26 (983 functions, 0 modifier, 1,545 condition — all three numbers verified exactly by this batch's census) folds into it.

items.evidence: horizon-world/src/loot.rs is written for the 26.3 loot format throughout: condition() (line 1368) reads only c["type"] (line 1377); modify() (line 1478) consults singular m["condition"] only (line 1488) while 26.1's 184 function-level condition lists are plural "conditions"; run() (line 1512) reads only f["type"] (line 1514) while 26.1's 1,404 functions all use the "function" key (default _ => {}, line 1927); table_raw() (line 2011) checks singular pool["condition"] (line 2018) and applies pool/table["modifier"] (lines 2029/2016) while 26.1 has 958 plural pool "conditions" arrays and 0 "modifier" keys; expand() (line 2070) checks singular entry["condition"] (line 2071) while 26.1's 247 entry lists are plural, so every entry passes its gate; create() (line 2121) applies entry["modifier"] (line 2123); the minecraft:tag arm reads entry["items"] (lines 2100/2136) while 26.1's tag entry uses the "name" field. Demonstrated with loot_fill (built 3m35s EXIT 0; 7 tables x seeds 1-5, evidence/loot_fill.log): chests/simple_dungeon every stack count 1 (set_count ignored); chests/ancient_city books stay plain minecraft:book (enchant_randomly ignored), leggings unenchanted; entities/zombie drops music_disc_lava_chicken on ALL 5 seeds (a killed_by_player + baby-on-chicken gated drop, unconditionally dropped); entities/creeper gunpowder x1 only (disc pool gate ignored but the tag entry yields nothing); blocks/stone -> minecraft:stone and blocks/diamond_ore -> minecraft:diamond_ore on all 5 seeds (exactly the 1.21.7 symptoms). Affects entity drops, chest/container loot, fishing, trial spawners and vaults. 0 additional gap checks: these tables are already counted under items.rs (B12-G01).

items.evidence: crafting.rs Ingredient::parse_object (line 123) requires a neoforge:ingredient_type or type key and returns None otherwise, so vanilla object forms ({"item": "..."}, {"tag": "..."}) fail to parse and the recipe is dropped. No vanilla 26.1 recipe uses object ingredients (2,391 string slots + 84 array slots whose 1,072 elements are all strings; the one apparent object slot is the firework star's shapes map, shape name -> string ingredient), so this affects only player datapack / mod recipes using the object form. Same code and same data property as 1.21.7's B12-G05 and 26.2's B12-G02.
items.title: Object-form recipe ingredients are rejected (datapack scope only)

items.evidence: crafting.rs:1739: time: v["cookingtime"].as_u64().unwrap_or(200) — a flat 200-tick default for all four cooking types. Vanilla 26.1's per-type defaults, verified by javap -c on the client jar (the int each recipe class passes to AbstractCookingRecipe.cookingMapCodec): smelting 200, blasting 100, smoking 100, campfire_cooking 100. A datapack blasting/smoking/campfire recipe without cookingtime would cook at 200 ticks instead of 100. All 116 vanilla cooking recipes carry explicit cookingtime (smelting 73, blasting 25, smoking 9, campfire 9), so no vanilla recipe is affected. The 26.2 tree uses per-type defaults (crafting.rs:1745-1759).
items.method: parser read + javap on cooking recipe classes + data scan

systemic_note: The prepared data is faithful — all 5,309 data-driven files byte-identical to the 26.1 jar, block-tags.json byte-faithful too. The 1.21.7 systemic finding (code reading the 26.x form of formats the version writes differently) DOES carry to 26.1: 26.1 writes the OLD loot forms (condition/function discriminators, plural conditions arrays, functions arrays, tag-entry name) while both engines in the 26.1 tree read the 26.3 forms (type, modifier, singular condition, tag items), and the 26.2 playtest fixes that taught the engines both forms were never carried to the 26.1 tree. Everything else in scope is clean: specials are data-driven, the effect table legitimately has 40 entries, and the recipe/advancement/tag/enchantment/damage loaders all read 26.1's forms correctly.
